chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Maceo Sheffield, the detective who loved musicians
summary: Sheffield arrested partygoers but let musicians go, used the catchphrases Every tub and It had to be you, and owned a saxophone and a trombone.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition

I want to talk about Sheffield. Sheffield was Maceo Sheffield, right?
Yeah, Maceo, yeah.
And he was a police officer in the Central Avenue area, right?

Well, he was a...he wasn't a...he was a po...had been a police officer but now he was doing detective work. He didn't wear a uniform no more, you know. That's the reason I told you, he used to go to all the dances and like in those days, they had a lot of parties. This's the reason they say he so fat. He used to go to the parties and everything, and then he'd...they'd be drinkin' goin' on, and he'd arrest them, you know--go to the party to have a good time, then he'll be...after awhile, he'd arrest them. But he always...if there's any musicians there, he'd turn them loose. He's...I told you he's crazy about musicians. And they would have these house-rent parties, you know, two, three, four o'clock in the morning, bootleggin'. He'd go there, and if the musicians, any of them in there that come from work, come drop by, he'd tell them to get out, and he'd pinch...[laughs]

Yeah! And "It had to be you!" that's what he
